title: Legacy quota-marker collision triggering silent throttles for mixed-hosted/dedicated tenants
creator: Alicia Grant
description:
Summary:
A subset of tenants that route across Hosted and Dedicated backends experienced opaque throttling (clients saw unexplained request failures and elevated tail latency) between 2026-03-01T02:00Z and 2026-03-01T05:30Z. Multiple enterprise customers escalated to support with the same pattern: sporadic 429s and timeouts despite apparent quota remaining in the dashboard.

Impact:
- Affected tenants: ~12 multi-tenant customers operating hybrid routing profiles (hosted -> dedicated fallback).
- Symptoms: intermittent silent drops (requests accepted by front proxy but rejected by downstream admission with no clear tenant credit decrement), elevated error rates for streaming responses, and increased retry storms from SDKs.
- Severity: P0 (customer outages & escalations).

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A legacy quota-marker format used by the private/dedicated admission controller collided with a new epoch-based reconciliation upgrade deployed in runtime-1.21. When a cross-region sticky-routing handoff occurred, the admission store saw two different markers for the same tenant shard: an old "marker_v1" token-bucket epoch and a new "marker_v2" reconciliation epoch. The reconciliation job treated the mismatch as a tombstone and temporarily froze token replenishment for the tenant shard, which caused the token-bucket admission code to start returning opaque rejections while metrics and dashboards still reported tokens present (stale cache).

How to reproduce (dev stack):
1) Configure a tenant with hybrid routing: primary Hosted, fallback Dedicated.
2) Inject a synthetic handoff event (simulate region failover) so the shard is re-anchored to a Dedicated host with a legacy marker present.
3) Run the reconciliation job v2 concurrently while sending steady traffic at 50% of tenant limit.
4) Observe admission rejections while dashboard token-count remains unchanged.

Immediate mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-03-01 03:10Z: Scoped rollback of reconciliation heuristics on Dedicated fleet -> dropped tombstone semantics. (mitigation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12187)
- 2026-03-01 03:30Z: Enabled per-tenant sticky routing for affected customers to avoid cross-backend handoffs during remediation window.
- 2026-03-01 04:00Z: Released emergency cache invalidation to ensure dashboards reflect live token counts (hotfix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2041).

Permanent fix plan:
1) Normalize marker formats during reconciliation: implement a compatibility layer that canonicalizes marker_v1 -> marker_v2 before tombstone/merge logic. (work item: this ticket)
2) Add a reconciliation dry-run mode and safety gate that prohibits freezing replenishment unless a quorum of shards indicate missing tokens.
3) Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate hybrid routing handoffs under reconciliation.
4) Improve observability: emit a "marker-collision" metric and a per-tenant reconciliation audit log entry surfaced in Console.

Implementation notes and design trade-offs:
- Option A (fast): strip tombstone behavior and fallback to conservative replenish -> lower chance of outage but may allow temporary slight overspend. Chosen for now as stopgap.
- Option B (safer long-term): implement canonicalization and quorum checks. Requires ~2 weeks and careful rollout (canary then global). This is the planned permanent route.

Rollout plan for permanent fix:
- Develop canonicalization patch + unit/integration tests (2 dev sprints).
- Canary on a small Dedicated pool (3 hosts) with synthetic traffic and tenant-simulators.
- Gradual ramp to all Dedicated and Private fleets with feature flags to disable canonicalization if unexpected regressions occur.

Monitoring & QA:
- New alert: marker_collision_rate > 0.01% for 5m -> Pager.
- Add e2e scenario to CI that repros previous outage pattern.
- QA checklist: reconciliation dry-run logs match canonicalized markers, no token freeze in heavy handoff simulation.

Stakeholders & comms:
- PM: Kiran Shah (notified)
- Support lead: Emilia Torres (coordinating customer comms)
- SRE: backend-oncall (rotation) monitoring escalation.

Links and artifacts:
- Initial incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/INCIDENTS/p1612345678000
- Hotfix PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12187, https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2041
- Internal playbook we used: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Quota+Incidents

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Canonicalization layer implemented and unit tested.
- Integration test added that covers hybrid handoff + reconciliation.
- Canary rollout completed without regression (2 days stable).
